open_points.subject: A01-2 and A01-3 repeat outcomes
open_points.text:
a check of stages (1) to (4) of A04 rule 6 fails, or m in {Room,
  ArtifactPointer} with its project archived => refused, store unchanged   -- A01-2
  f = current_facts(r)  => answer r, store unchanged   -- A01-3
open_points.question: Are A01-3 and A01-4 conditional on A01-2 being false, or do their implications apply independently? The invariant must make the ordered or mutually exclusive branches explicit.
options: Make A01-3 and A01-4 apply only after every A01-2 check passes.
Treat the implications independently, which requires resolving the resulting refused-versus-answer conflict.
open_points.default_guess: Make the branches ordered: apply A01-2 first, and consider fact equality only if it does not refuse.

witness.initial: Room R in project P carries request id K; session S no longer has P in its granted set; the retry supplies R's current facts.
events: Cabinet Kernel, for session S, repeats 'add a room' on P with request id K and equal facts.
outcomes: A01-2 and Required test 10 refuse the call as not found and disclose no room.
A01-3 answers the existing room because its current facts equal the supplied facts.
witness.observer: Cabinet Kernel sees either a not-found refusal or the room answer.

open_points.subject: 2026-11-24 security-review change account
open_points.question: How must this review account describe and assess the shown replacement of A09's normative refusal rule, which changes both its scope and removes the explicit guarantee that a change is undone?
options: State that A09's normative rule changed and record the security review of the new guarantee.
Restore the former normative guarantee so that the claim that no normative rule changed becomes true.
open_points.default_guess: State that A09 changed normatively and record the review result for the replacement rule.

open_points.subject: A21 review statement versus A17 listener checks
open_points.text: every start check stopping the start before any listener
open_points.question: Does this mean no listener is ever opened before every start check has passed, or only that no listener serves requests before all checks pass? It must agree with A17 rule 2, which opens the owner listener before attempting the service API listener and closes it if the latter fails.
options: Require that no listener is opened until all non-listener checks pass, while listener-opening checks may open and then close sockets without serving.
Require that no listener is opened before every check succeeds, which requires changing A17's specified listener-opening sequence.
Replace “before any listener” with “before any listener serves a request.”
open_points.default_guess: Replace the phrase with “before any listener serves a request,” preserving A17's explicit bind-and-close sequence.

witness.initial: The configuration and store pass every earlier check; the owner-interface address is available, but another process occupies the configured service-API endpoint.
events: Registry starts and reaches A17's listener checks.
Registry opens the owner-interface listener first.
Registry fails to open the service-API listener and stops the start.
outcomes: Under A17 rule 2, the owner listener was opened and is then closed; no request is served.
Under A21's literal statement, the start must stop before any listener is opened.
witness.observer: The host administrator or socket-binding instrumentation can observe whether the owner endpoint was temporarily bound.

Declare a specified representative subset sufficient and identify exactly which A01-2 branches it covers.

set_aside.subject: A12-2 meaning of an accepted change
set_aside.text: accepted change of x other than its end => version(x)' = version(x) + 1   -- A12-2
set_aside.question: Does “change of x” mean an accepted action intended to change the session, or only an accepted action that actually changes its granted set, active project or pending request?
options: Add an actual-state-change condition; accepted no-op actions leave the version unchanged.
Make every accepted access-changing action move the version, including a no-op grant, and revise rule 2 and Required test 3.
set_aside.default_guess: Add an actual-state-change condition, matching normative rule 2 and Required test 3.

witness.initial: Session S is at access version 1 and already has project P in its granted set.
events: The owner grants P to S again while stating version 1.
outcomes: Normative rule 2 and Required test 3 accept the no-op and leave the version at 1.
A12-2 can be read to require version 2 because the grant is an accepted change action other than an end.
witness.observer: The owner and Cabinet Kernel see version 1 or version 2 on the next access read.
